answer: Each identity locks an 85-credit bond and insures one nebula site against a plume event, paying a plume premium. The first same-funder site costs 22, the kth costs 22+9(k-1), so the 1000th costs 9013 and 1000 fake sites cost 4,517,500 plus 85,000 locked. A mirror ledger keeps a mirror record of each site, and auditors pay only on a matching record; a missing site, reused site key, or mismatched mirror record burns the bond. A rented-site ring fails because shared operator mirror records expose divergent keys. An honest agent pays 22 once and reclaims its bond after a clean epoch.
